claim: Every path through query_database_impl_with_widgets that finishes an agent turn reaches the new open_error check. No earlier return (an empty answer, a starter UI or widget request, a conversation or profile branch) sends a success result before the check runs.

When the memory-unavailable AgentRunError is raised, the failed turn is not recorded in the conversation store as a successful assistant answer. Later turns in the same conversation do not inherit an answer that was produced without saved memory.

The server.py docstring says that when the memory store cannot be opened, the call returns an error result whose message is `Memory store unavailable: ...` after the `Error executing tool` prefix. This must hold on the show_details-off path too, where server.py re-raises AgentRunError and FastMCP's Tool.run builds the error text.

open_error is typed `BaseException | None`, but _get_client records only `Exception` subclasses. If a BaseException that is not an Exception escapes PersistentClient (for example a CancelledError when the open runs in an executor or task), it is not recorded and does not clear a stale earlier record.

The test docstring claims a workflow-handled message makes no model call and no store open. The stub-based test never checks that no open was attempted, so the claim needs a falsification attempt against the real workflow handler.

test_cleared_open_error_returns_normal_result asserts only that memory_info is not None. Acceptance criterion 3 requires `_meta["sqllens/memory_info"]` to still report search hits and misses, so the test does not pin hit and miss counts from _memory_card(hit_count=2, top_similarity=0.9).
